latest_findings.claim: At N=64 (4 layers, d_model=64, 3000 steps, e<=0.5, seeds 20-21), the final layer-1 force margin is 0.215 in seed 20 (R2 0.726 vs control 0.511), inside the predicted [0.07, 0.22] band, but 0.261 in seed 21 (R2 0.737 vs control 0.476). Seed 21's value is above the 0.23 cutoff and inside the N=16 range of 0.236-0.275, so the predicted monotonic drop in force with N is not shown. The accel_step half of the hypothesis holds in both seeds: layer-4 R2 is 0.935-0.938 against controls of 0.770-0.791 (raw margin 0.147-0.165), which gives a headroom-normalized margin of 0.70-0.72. That is inside [0.62, 0.77] and matches the N=16 and N=256 arms, while normalized force is lower at 0.44-0.50.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs completed all 3000 steps (val_mse_ratio 0.0148-0.0149) and every margin clears its required_margin. Spreads are small for force (0.009-0.041) and accel_step (0.009-0.014). The verdict is inconclusive because the force prediction splits across seeds: one seed is just inside the band and the other is in N=16 territory. Taken together, the data look more like a step than a gradient: force at N=64 (0.21-0.26) is close to N=16 (0.24-0.28), and most of the drop to 0.03-0.04 happens between N=64 and N=256. The 0.047 seed-to-seed gap here is as large as the N=16 vs N=64 difference, so two seeds cannot fix where N=64 sits. Force is also still rising at step 3000 in both seeds (+0.006 to +0.008 per 500 steps), so the comparison depends on training length. The flat normalized accel_step result is consistent across seeds and with the other arms. Seeds 22-23 at N=64, plus an N=128 arm, would settle the shape of the force curve. If both new N=64 seeds land at 0.23 or above, the result would change to 'refuted (step)'. If both land at 0.22 or below, it would change to 'supported'.

latest_findings.claim: In both seeds, force beats its best-of-5 control at the end of training, forms well after accel_step, and keeps strengthening while accel_step levels off. Its gain from step 1000 to step 5000 falls short of the pre-registered >= 0.08 bar. (a) Final force margin is 0.232 (seed 73, R2 0.776 vs control 0.544) and 0.218 (seed 78, R2 0.709 vs 0.490), against a required 0.1. Final accel_step margin is 0.177 / 0.175 (R2 0.964 / 0.967 vs control 0.787 / 0.792). (b) Read from the trajectory, accel_step persistently forms at step 100 in both seeds. Force persistently forms at step 300-350 in seed 73 (the 300 checkpoint rounds to exactly 0.100) and step 350 in seed 78, a lag of 200-250 steps. (c) From step 1000 to 5000, force gains +0.078 (seed 73, 0.154 to 0.232) and +0.063 (seed 78, 0.155 to 0.218), both under the 0.08 bar. accel_step gains only +0.019 / +0.015 (<= 0.04, as predicted). Measured from step 500 instead, the force gains are +0.109 / +0.086, which reproduces seeds 74/75. Headroom-normalized, accel_step still leads force in both seeds (0.83 vs 0.51, 0.84 vs 0.43).
latest_findings.confidence_note: Both runs finished all 5000 steps (no early stop). Neither branch fits. Both seeds meet (a) and (b) and the accel_step half of (c), but the force gain from step 1000 to 5000 misses 0.08: narrowly in seed 73 (0.078, which rounding cannot lift above 0.08), and clearly in seed 78 (0.063). This is the reverse of the pre-registered 'late strengthening without late formation' case: here force forms late, and its strengthening after step 1000 is real but smaller than predicted. Most of the late force gain happens between steps 500 and 1500 and then slows (about +0.004 to +0.012 per 500 steps after step 2000). The two seeds agree on every sub-criterion. The verdict is inconclusive because the outcome falls between the pre-registered branches, not because the seeds disagree. Three things limit interpretation. First, probes_final.formed_at_step for force is 400 in both seeds, while the trajectory shows persistent crossing at 300-350. This is another formed_at_step-vs-trajectory lag (cf. q-20261012-032843-df65), so formation is quoted from the trajectory. Second, from steps 700-750 onward, force's best layer moves from layer 4 to layer 1, the layer where distance peaks (distance margin 0.22-0.26, also still rising). So the late force gain may be a sharper 1/r^2 read of the distance code rather than an m2-weighted force. Without a residualized force target, these cannot be told apart. Third, data_seed is fixed at 0. What would change the verdict: a pre-registered window starting at step 500 would make this 'supported'. A residualized force target (distance and accel_step regressed out) that drops below 0.1 would reclassify the late gain as a distance proxy.

latest_findings.claim: At e in [0, 0.75], seeds 70-72 reach a final raw layer-4 accel_step R2 of 0.753, 0.746 and 0.752. All three fall in the predicted [0.66, 0.77] window. Their best-of-5 controls (0.471, 0.487, 0.463) lie between the seed-matched e<=0.7 values (0.54-0.56) and e<=0.85 values (0.26-0.27). The margins are 0.283, 0.259 and 0.290, which normalise to 0.51-0.54 of headroom. The pre-registered criterion is met, but R2 is not where linear interpolation put it: it sits about 0.03 above the predicted ~0.72. The drop is therefore uneven: about 0.05 of R2 is lost from e<=0.7 (~0.80) to e<=0.75, then about 0.19 from e<=0.75 to e<=0.85 (~0.56), roughly 0.095 per 0.05 of e. Force also beats its control in all 3 seeds, but more weakly: R2 0.443, 0.360 and 0.470 against controls 0.333, 0.234 and 0.324, giving margins of 0.110-0.146 and normalised margins of 0.16-0.22. Force forms late, at steps 300-500, and is still rising at step 600. accel_step forms at steps 50-100 and has levelled off. accel_step leads force on both raw and normalised margin in every seed. val_mse_ratio is 0.143-0.147.
latest_findings.confidence_note: All 3 seeds completed 600 of 600 steps and satisfy every expected-if-true condition independently. The criteria were pre-registered, and the result passes them. Even so, the substantive claim that the drop is gradual is only weakly supported. R2 of about 0.75 sits near the upper edge of the window and 0.03 below the 0.78 refutation bar. The loss per 0.05 of e is about 0.05 between 0.7 and 0.75 but averages about 0.095 between 0.75 and 0.85. That pattern suggests the drop steepens above 0.75 rather than being uniform. The e<=0.7 and e<=0.85 comparison values come from other experiments, which used the same seeds, data_seed 0, N=64 and 600 steps. I quote them from the hypothesis and did not recompute them here. All runs share data_seed 0. Training stopped at 600 steps, and accel_step R2 was still creeping up (+0.002 to +0.005 over the last 100 steps). Three things would change the reading: an e<=0.8 arm landing near 0.70 (which would make the curve smooth), or one landing near 0.60 (which would put most of the loss between 0.75 and 0.8); or a second data_seed giving R2 >= 0.78 at e<=0.75, which would push this result toward refuted.

latest_findings.claim: With data_seed 1 (seeds 75-77, N=64, e<=0.5, 600 steps), the core pattern from data_seed 0 holds in all 3 seeds, but one pre-registered timing criterion fails. The best-layer (layer 4) accel_step margin is 0.149-0.168: R2 0.914-0.918 against controls of 0.750-0.766, about 0.64-0.67 of the possible headroom. The force margin stays below 0.1 at 0.085-0.099: R2 0.606-0.643 against controls of 0.509-0.545, about 0.19-0.22 of headroom. accel_step forms persistently at steps 80, 90 and 120, and every one of these is before val_mse_ratio first drops below 1 (step 180 in all 3 seeds). Seed 77's formation at step 120 is outside the predicted [60, 110] window but inside the [50, 130] tolerance in the falsification criteria.
latest_findings.confidence_note: This is not a refutation: none of the expected-if-false conditions holds in 2 or more seeds. It is also not fully supported, because the expected-if-true outcome required all 3 formation steps to fall in [60, 110], and seed 77 missed by one checkpoint (margin 0.094 at step 110, 0.102 at step 120). Formation steps were read from the trajectory as the first checkpoint after which the margin stays at or above 0.1 (strict >=). For all 3 seeds they match probes_final.formed_at_step (80, 90, 120). The accel_step control R2 (0.750-0.766) falls inside the range seen with data_seed 0 (0.709-0.778). The early force transient also replicates: margin 0.11-0.19 at steps 10-30, then 0-0.04 by steps 40-70. Two things limit the 'force does not beat control' half of the claim. First, the force margin is close to the bar (seed 75: 0.0988 unrounded). Second, it is still rising at step 600, by about +0.01 per 100 steps after step 400, while accel_step has levelled off. That part of the claim is therefore specific to 600 steps of training; longer runs would likely push force past 0.1. This experiment covers only one new dataset. A second data_seed, or a pooled look at all N=64, e<=0.5 seeds, showing formation in [60, 130] would turn this into 'supported'. A force margin above 0.1 at 600 steps on another data_seed would weaken the force half of the claim.

latest_findings.claim: In one seed (75; 4 layers, d_model=128, 5000 steps, e <= 0.5, m2 in [0.1, 1]), force beats its best-of-5 control at the end of training. Force R2 is 0.748 at layer 1 vs control 0.539, a margin of 0.209 against a required 0.1. Its margin roughly doubles after the first checkpoint, from 0.102 at step 500 to 0.209 at step 5000, while val_mse_ratio falls from 0.39 to 0.005. accel_step stays ahead throughout: R2 0.952 at layer 4 vs control 0.762, margin 0.190, and it gains only 0.029 after step 500. Normalized by headroom, accel_step leads at the end (0.80 vs 0.45 for force), but force's normalized margin roughly doubles from about 0.21 at step 500, while accel_step's rises only from about 0.68. The 'forms late' part is not supported. In the trajectory, force is already at the bar at step 500 (0.102), the same first checkpoint where accel_step forms. formed_at_step = 1000 is again one checkpoint behind the trajectory.
latest_findings.confidence_note: Only one seed ran, but the prediction needed both seeds, so replication is not possible here. The results are mixed against the prediction. Two parts held in this seed: the final force margin (0.209 >= 0.1) and the late gain (+0.107 >= 0.08). Neither refutation condition was met. The formation-timing part failed: the trajectory reaches the bar at step 500, not at step >= 1000, and 500-step checkpoints cannot tell whether force crosses before or after accel_step within the first 500 steps. The step-500 force margin (0.102) only just clears the bar, and controls are fixed per run, so 'persistent from 500' is fragile. Force peaks at layer 1, the same layer as distance (R2 0.983, margin 0.184), and its best layer moves between layers 1-4 over training. So the late gain may be a sharpened nonlinear read of distance rather than an m2-weighted force code, and this probe cannot tell those apart. The large late force gain does fit the earlier single-control runs, which reached about 0.22, and the companion seed-74 result (f-20261013-000424-5488), so the earlier 0.22 margins are not purely a single-control artifact. A second seed at the same config would strengthen this, especially with 50-step checkpoints through step 1000 and the force margin after regressing out distance. The verdict would move to refuted if that seed's final force margin is < 0.1, or if force stays above 0.1 after distance is regressed out but without late growth.
